briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for September 5, 2026. Based on the climate-related news gathered today, we will delve into the severity of the global climate crisis, the efforts being made to address it, and the challenges we face.

sections.title: 🔴 Climate Disasters and Humanitarian Crises Sweeping the Globe
sections.content: In Nepal, large-scale floods have continued for ten days, resulting in over 1,300 deaths and more than 5,500 missing persons, with international aid, including rescue efforts by Korean teams, underway [6, 16, 17, 18]. The head of Caritas Nepal has described the damage caused by climate change to the Nepali people as a 'grave injustice,' warning of a humanitarian crisis [25]. In South Korea's Chungcheong region, extreme weather phenomena such as intensifying heatwaves and torrential rains are becoming commonplace [1, 3], and globally, warnings continue about the worsening wildfire season due to fossil fuels, potentially accompanied by new viral threats [28, 30]. Notably, Sydney is facing an extreme fire risk, with an unprecedented high temperature of 33 degrees Celsius in early September raising the possibility of the warmest spring since the mid-1800s [41].

sections.title: ⚠️ Intensifying Scientific Warnings and Regional Impacts of Climate Change
sections.content: Observations that the glaciers in Northwest Greenland have decreased in thickness by an average of 5.4 meters over the past 13 years, and that their melting rate would double with just one more degree of warming, present a serious warning to us [19]. This aligns with the melting phenomenon of Himalayan glaciers, which has been warned about since 2007 [20], and Europe has already become the fastest-warming continent on Earth [37]. Climate change is reshaping migration patterns for residents in areas like Florida [22], and even threatening the livelihoods of Colorado ranchers, leading to calls for accountability [24]. Greenhouse gases are disrupting climate connections between the Indian and Pacific Oceans [39], and the severity of the issue is becoming evident on a global scale, with the question of responsibility for such extreme weather events being discussed internationally [38, 40].

sections.title: 🌱 Domestic and International Efforts for Carbon Neutrality and Renewable Energy Transition
sections.content: Domestic and international efforts to address the climate crisis are actively underway. Gyeongsangnam-do Province is strengthening its climate response, including assessing climate risks before designing public buildings [2], and Gimpo City is encouraging citizen participation by hosting an AI-powered climate response short-form content contest [5]. Nowon-gu District and Hwaseong Special City have pledged leading roles by participating in citizen declarations and joint resolutions, aiming for carbon neutrality by 2026 and 2030, respectively [8, 11]. Furthermore, Korea East-West Power is holding renewable energy workshops, and as Energy Storage Systems (ESS) emerge as a key means to alleviate instability in renewable energy grids [13, 14], the spread of citizen-participatory energy transition models, such as mandating solar panel installation in public parking lots, is also being promoted [15]. New York's Central Park, adapting to climate change and contributing to mitigating the urban heat island effect, is also a positive example [23, 34].

sections.title: 🌍 Challenges and Debates in Responding to the Climate Crisis
sections.content: Many challenges and debates persist in responding to the climate crisis. Domestic editorials emphasize the need for a control tower to effectively respond to the climate crisis [4], and rising labor costs in the power grid sector are impacting renewable energy investments, acting as a new obstacle [12]. Global efforts for marine decarbonization are stagnating despite the accelerating impacts of climate change [27], and there are strong criticisms regarding the fact that climate change deniers still gain airtime despite the unfolding crisis [35]. Meanwhile, controversies are being raised regarding the causes of floods in the Himalayan region, attributing them not only to climate change but also to indiscriminate development [6, 32]. This highlights a period of active discussion on various perspectives concerning the climate change narrative [31].

briefing.closing: Today's briefing has highlighted the reality of the climate crisis facing the world, the diverse efforts being made to combat it, and the complex challenges that need to be addressed. Reaffirming that a sustainable future for humanity is difficult to secure without immediate and multifaceted responses to climate change, we urge continuous attention and action from all of us. This concludes today's climate briefing.
